content_html_sanitized:
Analysis by Richard Cowan
Posted October 13, 2003

For several years, I have been trying to warn my Canadian friends about the prohibitionist counterattack that was being mounted by DEAland's agents in the Canadian police apparatus.
See
The Next Prime Minister of Canada Talks War On Us. Looming Prohibitionist Counterattack in Canada Proves Need for International Debate On Cannabis Prohibition.
and links

It is now apparent that they have so frightened the invertebrates in Ottawa that a bill that was once being sold as decriminalization is now being sold as getting tough.
See
Canadian Prime Minister Commits To Decriminalization Soon Just 23 Years After He First Said He Was In Favor. It Was A Good Idea Then, But John Conroy Thinks It May Be Dangerous Now.
and
Canadian Prime Minister Says He Has Been In Favor Of Decrim Since 1980. How Time Flies When You Are In Power. Possession Law Hostage to Medical Cannabis. Another Deadline On Taking Care of Patients.

The originally proposed limit on personal possession has been dropped from 30 grams to 15, and may be cut to 10 or even 5 grams. There is also talk of giving the police discretion as to whether their victims will be fined or arrested, thereby making decrim a police option, not the law. The prohibitionists are also urging escalating fines and jail time for repeat offenders.
From 2000 see
Toronto Police Chief Supports Decrim -- At the Option of The Narks And " Education Or Treatment Programs " For Marijuana Users. The Therapeutic Police State. -- 2 Articles

In exchange for this liberalization the prohibitionists are also calling for sharply increasing the penalties for growing, and even mandatory minimums, while DEAland judges are denouncing them as disastrous failures. Canada has no other such laws, thus the penalties for growing would be more severe than for child-molestation.

So far the Canadian anti-prohibitionist media have not picked up on this bait-and-switch. The Vancouver Sun, which has endorsed complete legalization, praised the originally proposed concept of decriminalization, as have some other papers. Sooner or later, they will wake up.

On October 7th, the Ontario Court of Appeal ruled that Health Canada's requirements for medical users were too stringent, and also said that medical growers could charge for growing and grow for more than one patient. This was seen as a victory for the compassion clubs.

They also reinstated the law against possession in Ontario, which had been suspended by a lower court because it did not allow for medical users.
From 1999 see
Canada Health Minister Won't Challenge Medical Marijuana Ruling:
" We're going to start making marijuana available to people for medical purposes by the end of June "
and
In Canada Only the Government Has Difficulty Getting Marijuana.
However, " Canadians who want to take part in a clinical trial
will find application forms on Health Canada's Web Site "

This was seen as a defeat for recreational users. However, both the victories and the defeat are less serious than they may seem.

While the Ontario Court of Appeal did reaffirm the Constitutional right to medical access (a very important difference from DEAland), it still left too many hurdles for patients. It dropped the requirement for a recommendation from two specialists, but still required that one specialist make such a recommendation. Inasmuch as it often takes six months to see a specialist under Canada's underfunded socialized medicine program, and doctors are often reluctant to make any such recommendation, this is still an entirely unreasonable requirement. If the judges were in pain, would they want to wait six months?
See
Ethical Failure Of Cannabis Prohibition. Tragedy And Farce. Using the Patients To Protect Prohibition. Analysis by Richard Cowan

As for the rest of the medical part of the ruling, the court simply told Health Canada to come up with a licensing provision for medical growers. That means that Health Minister Ann McLellan (John Walters in drag) will take as long as possible to come up with some more unworkable requirements, such as the million dollar bond that was required in their original tender for a monopoly grower.
See
Canadian Health Minister Seeks Asylum In DEAland; Says Making Her Think About Medical Cannabis Constitutes Torture. In DC They Don't Allow That Sort of Thing. Thinking, That Is.
and
Canada's New Decriminalization Bill To Be Delayed After Justice Minister's Trip to Washington, and Health Minister's Trip to the Marvelous World Of Marijuana Make-Believe. John Walters In Drag?

McLellan has done everything in her power to block sick and dying Canadians from being able to exercise their right to have an effective medicine.

On the other hand, the temporary loophole under which possession was legalized in Ontario, and by extension in a few other provinces, was always just a temporary loophole. If the courts had let it stand, it was certain that the Parliament would move to reinstate the law.

After the Court of Appeals ruling, Justice Minister Martin Cauchon struck a much more ominous note. In a television interview, he completely changed the tone of the party line on the proposed changes in the cannabis laws.

Instead of talking about " sparing young people the stigma of a criminal record, " he emphasized that this was NOT decriminalization, and made very clear that the new system of fines for users was intended to intensify enforcement, and the most important part of the bill was the sharp increase in penalties for growing.

While that is the obvious truth, for a change, the sudden candor and almost vicious tone indicates that it is " no-more-Mr.-Nice-Guy " time in Ottawa. It was a blunt declaration of war on the cannabis communities. The only question is whether we will mount an effective defense or just get rolled over again.

To add urgency to the matter, the government has recalled the House committee to hold hearings on the new law this week. If they succeed in fast-tracking the bill, we will be at a major disadvantage. We need to respond immediately, and demand a real debate on the subject.
See
Canadian Justice Minister Calls for National Debate On Cannabis Policies And Begins It By Debating Himself. Phony Decrim Bill May Be Used As Cover To Increase Penalties for Growing.
and
We Live In Interesting Times: Chaos in Cannabis Prohibition Around the World. Does John Walters Really Want A National Debate on Marijuana Prohibition?
and
Canada Discovers The Netherlands As Senator Nolin Goes To Washington. What Bush/Ashcroft/Walters Really Fear: An Honest Debate On The Issues. We Are Winning!

Unfortunately, the Canadian parliamentary system is increasingly undemocratic. Former Liberal Prime Minister John Turner recently complained, " The power of the House of Commons is a myth "

Canadians of all stripes are concerned about what is being called the democratic deficit. The Liberal Party (not really liberal but a cross between Tony Blair's New Labour and Bill Clinton's New Democrats) has a stranglehold on Canadian politics because the two conservative parties are incapable of getting their acts together, jointly or severally, which may be just as well. In any case, the process in Ottawa is completely dominated by the most ignorant prohibitionists.

Ironically, that may be our best hope. We are now dependent on the stupidity of our enemies (a very reliable force) to save us from the duplicity and cravenness of our friends. With any luck the prohibitionists will delay the bill and scare the next Prime Minister into doing nothing.

All is not lost, by any means.

First, the Canadian Supreme Court is expected to rule before the end of the year, give or take a few months. (I am going out on a limb, but I predict that they will legalize possession, but defer to Parliament on sales.)
See
How Canada Could Have A Major Impact On The World By Legalizing Cannabis. More Than Its Own Sovereignty Is At Stake. What Washington Really Fears Is Freedom. Supreme Court Cases Make This Urgent.

Second, the Canadian Senate might not assent to a really bad bill. The appointed upper chamber usually does not exercise its veto power, but a bill that was too greatly at variance with both the Senate and House committee recommendations might run into enough difficulty to embarrass the government.
See
Canadian Senator Stars At NORML Conference As DEAland Threatens Retaliation, Again. Rightwing Think Tank Cited As Semi-Official Source. Is Canada Still Too White To Invade? Bad Neighbor Policy?

Third, speaking of stupidity, John Walters attacked the outgoing Canadian Prime Minister for joking that he might try marijuana after he retires, saying Canadians are ashamed of him.

The Globe and Mail, one of Canada's two national newspapers, denounced the Czar in an editorial today:

U.S. anti-drug czar John Walters makes no secret of his intense dislike for Canadian moves toward more relaxed marijuana laws. He objects to decriminalizing pot use and doesn't even want the stuff distributed to sick people for medicinal reasons.

Mr. Walters is so irate he can't see the humour in Prime Minister Jean Chrétien's recent remarks about perhaps trying pot in retirement once it becomes legal. He told a Washington think-tank that Canadians are " ashamed " of their Prime Minister.

And he went even further, calling Canada " the one place in the hemisphere where things are going the wrong [way] " in the war on drugs.

That's in contrast to his high praise for Colombia, which has managed to reduce coca cultivation by 15 per cent in the past year. That doesn't make much of a dent in world supply and isn't much of a return on the more than $25-billion (U.S.) handed over to Colombia in the past three years specifically to combat cocaine production and trafficking.

Nor can Mr. Walters point to any great victories on U.S. soil, where strong demand remains the biggest problem, and where several states are following the Canadian example of looking for alternatives to unrealistic penalties for simple marijuana possession.

The man plainly needs a rest. Perhaps a Valium would help.

The editorial indicates that Canadians do not really want their laws made in Washington. Unfortunately, it also shows a degree of ignorance about how much of a liar Walters really is.
See
As Canada Moves Toward Some Form Of Decriminalization, Canadian Narks and Walters Escalate Lying. The New Math. Canada Replaces Mexico As Leading Supplier of Cannabis. And If You Believe That

In DEAland it is not just that strong demand remains the biggest problem but also production. DEAland is almost certainly the world's largest producer of methamphetamines, and it has probably surpassed Mexico as the world's largest producer of marijuana. (I hope to write on that subject soon.)

Moreover, several states are not just following the Canadian example of looking for alternatives to unrealistic penalties for simple marijuana possession. For more that 25 years, they have had various forms of decriminalization laws that are generally more liberal than the proposed Canadian law. More than 100 million Americans live in decrim states.

Fourth, if the Parliament does pass harsher penalties against growing, there will be a public backlash, especially in BC, and from the anti-prohibitionist press.
From 2000 see
Poll Shows B.C. Residents Reject DEAland Pressure To Increase Penalties on Marijuana Growing.

Fifth, the BC Courts are simply not going to go along with DEAland-style penalties. The judges know better, and the province is having to close hospitals, jails and courts because it is so heavily in debt. Moreover, the province depends on the marijuana industry to support the economy in many areas. Although police estimates on the size of the industry are probably exaggerations, if they are accurate it would merely prove the absurdity of even trying to eliminate it. In other words, the bigger the problem, the stupider the crackdown would be.

I have written an article that will be in the next issue of CannabisHealth.com that should be available online soon, urging the Canadian cannabis communities to unite and demand an international debate on the issues. It remains to be seen if that will happen. The anti-prohibitionist movement in Canada is more fragmented and underfunded than even DEAland's.

However, this proposed new law must be seen for what it really is. This is not just an attack on the cannabis communities, but a major escalation of the police state in Canada. All around the world the Bush regime is using the drug war and the war on cannabis in particular to create a global fascist police network in collusion with the UN.
See
America Sentenced to Life In Prison For Marijuana. Really! Another One We Couldn't Make Up. And As Usual, It Is Even Worse for Others. DEAland's War On Cannabis Disastrous for Poor Countries.
and
UN Agency Tries to Get Swazis To Switch From Insangu To Hemp Cultivation. Weird, And Sad, But Interesting.

Oh dear, does that sound too extreme? Too uncool? Certainly, warnings about fascism are often misused, but consider that recently, the Conservative columnist George Will wrote, (T)he Cold War may come to be remembered as a parenthesis in a much longer war against the remarkable resilience and insufficiently understood variousness of fascism.
See
Canada Exports A Little Reefer to DEAland. Imports A Lot of Reefer Madness. A Bad Balance of Trade. Canadian Taxpayers Are Being Lied to At Their Own Expense, But It May Also Cost Them Their Freedom.

I do not think that a real escalation of the war on us will work in Canada. Sadly, more innocent people may be hurt in proving this, but the very nature of Canadian society is about to be put to the test.

Paradoxically, the true friends of freedom will have to take the cannabis issue seriously in order to understand that this struggle is about much more than cannabis. It is about everyone's freedom.
See
A Tale of Two Canadas. Debate Over Medical Cannabis Refugees Is A Part of Struggle for National Identity. If They Learn What Has Happened to America, They May Reject That Fate For Themselves.
